reviews.assessment: Read all 973 lines, including later refinements rather than treating the early status header as the source's final word. The manuscript explains the selected Cauchy model and binary law, equicausal local QME, bounded-chart quartet/formal-positivity assumptions, parent-state restriction versus arbitrary marginal gluing, compact Hilbert-BV Hodge and finite-shell regulators, Kato common-boundary/gap transport, collar and auxiliary sign-flip limits, the first-order Yang-Mills complex, and direct Lorentzian smoothing with modified Ward identities and a formal causal-renormalization bridge. Older route counts are historical, not current completion counts. Canonical operational and free/local results are retained; a selected interacting fixed-coupling continuum and universal apparatus/actualization law are not inferred. The no-count 'propagator' wording at lines 577-579 is corrected as an effect/amplitude distinction, with separate erratum guidance, not a downgrade of the output theorem.

Explained as an established operational model on the declared geometric/causal background: the complex six-dimensional finite fiber has P/Q ranks two/four, while the Cauchy Hilbert space is generally infinite dimensional. The finite symbol fixes the bounded internal reduced semigroup, minimal Fock dilation, and comparison of instruments. The one-anchor rate log(448) and physical clock calibration are separated. Normal-state/effect/instrument data are explicit; equality of unread channels does not identify the apparatus. The general reconstruction remains conditional without reopening this canonical model.

Explained the selected framed globally hyperbolic spin-preserving category, massless rank-24 Dirac carrier, P/Q ranks 8/16 and chiral ranks 4/8, causal CAR construction, graded locality/even observable locality, time-slice property and Hadamard state existence. Omitted mass and gauge zero-order terms define this free tier and do not predict that physical masses vanish. No preferred vacuum or identification of inequivalent global spin structures is claimed. The packet's assertion that quasifree states form a convex set is false in general; a two-mode occupation-mixture example explains the correction to a quasifree Hadamard class or ordinary Hadamard convex hull. Net, locality and positivity statements remain intact; shared erratum required for that wording only.

Imported the local all-orders formal perturbative QME at the accepted finite SM content and profile-dependent coefficients. The text states on-shell globally hyperbolic chart, compact-support interaction, equicausal functional domain, causal time-ordering, local BRST and Adler-Bardeen hypotheses; the five perturbative anomaly coefficients and faithful Z6 bordism obstruction vanish in the stated model. Nilpotent quantum BV differential, degree-zero physical algebra and gauge-fixing independence are kept at formal/local scope. Later source-status refinements explain formal state positivity under the H1/quartet assumptions and restriction from a common parent. This neither repeats finite Yukawa/EW derivations nor supplies arbitrary overlapping state gluing or a fixed-coupling continuum theory.

Explained the physical gauge Weyl, four-real-component Higgs Weyl and rank-48 chiral CAR minimal tensor product, with compact-gauge/even restriction, free positive states, GNS and local von Neumann objects. Higgs/fermion quasifree local quasi-equivalence and the gauge constraint-preserving implementable Hilbert-Schmidt orbit are distinguished. Later finite interacting regulators and norm-Duhamel first-tangent comparisons retain observable transport by the renormalization map; first jets do not determine higher composite-observable jets. Normalized determinants remove an absolute phase but not transverse currents, crossings or disconnected gluing. The smooth flat-coupling example explains noninjectivity of formal jets without excluding future analytic or genuinely nonperturbative completion theorems.

Imported the exact realization of a supplied unitary bundle/connection as a finite-matrix projector module and the differential/Hessian intertwining on its range with transported metrics and domains. Finite matrix size is not a finite Fourier cutoff; ambient vectors outside the projector range are not new physical modes. The shared flat line and external flag are separated from parallel subbundles of an irreducible stable HYM bundle with scalar commutant. A winding-isometry cutoff example and Schur-Feshbach example explain why raw cutoffs or closed cost pullbacks are not automatically reducing operator isometries. This is a universal compiler for supplied data, not selection of the physical nonzero-Chern HYM endpoint.

Explained metric-unitarized transition functions, partition-of-unity projector blocks and the connection correction Gamma = U(A-A0)U*. The Grassmann connection alone need not equal the input connection; the correction supplies exact differential naturality. Cover/partition changes give partial-unitary equivalent presentations, not additional physical sources. Central phase cancellation on the adjoint does not trivialize a twisted fundamental bundle; the ordinary rank-102 deformation complex is not the finite 27-dimensional carrier. The range/domain and cutoff qualifications are part of the contextual use, not an extra unproved physical-naturalness claim.

Explained the nonlinear Hermitian-three-by-three strain coordinates (d,r), the omitted triangle-phase invariant and seven-dimensional generic invariant quotient, and the character obstruction to replacing them by a linear equivariant root-plane identification. On the regular all-edge-nonzero stratum, with a positive gapped physical Hessian on the declared harmonic complement and invertible retained covariance, the shorted Hessian is (J G_perp J*) inverse. It is a constrained minimum, not an arbitrary slice Hessian; TT reduction must occur before inversion. The later support-stratified result supplies the boundary qualification. No physical Hessian or spectral gap is selected by the coordinate theorem.

Imported all eight edge-support strata, derivative ranks 3+|S| with multiplicities 1,3,3,1, and the target orthant. At absent edges the first derivative of squared modulus vanishes; the normal second-order constraint produces a degree-one constrained value function in outward strain, not an ordinary quadratic Hessian on six unrestricted boundary coordinates. The elementary r=t^2, cost=t^2/2 example makes the distinction readable. Tangential Green shorting stays valid on its proper image. Full six-dimensional derivative rank or the proposed full local complex symmetry already forces the top stratum, so no independent regularity obligation is reintroduced under those stronger inputs. This is the source's existing boundary correction, not a newly discovered theorem defect.

Explained that a connected three-sheet cover with full S3 monodromy has trivial deck centralizer, rather than a global deck-S3 action. The correct strain object is the associated local system with R3 plus R3 fiber; Reynolds averaging gives parallel rank-two/rank-four projectors. The central sign of the nonsplit binary lift acts trivially on the quadratic strain representation, so its twelve-term average agrees with the six-term S3 average, without settling spinor Spin/Spin-c data. Naturality of a reduced Green operator follows only when the operator, domains and harmonic complement are themselves monodromy-natural. The later shared-root C4 refinement is discussed additively, not as reopening the retired deck requirement.

Explained the restriction of shared Z64 characters 1 and 33 to the same C4 character and the determinant-twisted sheet/edge identification producing J_DE squared = -I. On two real standard TT copies, S3-invariant covariance has a symmetric two-by-two multiplicity block; commuting with J_DE forces zero mixing and equal diagonal entries. Thus no additional TT-shape inputs remain once physical invariance is actually established. That physical nonzero-Chern HYM/Hessian invariance or direct TT-block computation remains open. Orthant, marked Fu-Yau and direct-unital-adjoint exclusions are stated precisely and do not revoke the canonical complex structure or the exact symbol-level order-four map.

source.exact_text:
The old paper used a bounded pullback as if it automatically preserved
closedness.  That is false without additional control.

corrections.defect: This incorrectly denies closedness of bounded pullback on the full preimage domain.
corrections.correction: For bounded I and closed semibounded q, q(Ix,Iy) on I^{-1}D(q) is closed and semibounded. A sufficiently shifted pullback norm is equivalent to ||x||^2+q_beta(Ix); its Cauchy sequences converge downstairs and in the upstairs form norm, with limits identified by boundedness. Domain density and reducing-operator identification remain separate.
corrections.bounded_explanation: On l2, q(v)=sum n^2|v_n|^2 and I:C->l2, Ic=(c/n), give preimage domain {0}. The existing closed reducing-isometry proposition is retained.
corrections.consumer_guidance: Do not repeat the v4 objection to closedness. State full-preimage domain, density and operator/domain reduction explicitly. This correction is not a claim that a cost pullback or arbitrary cutoff is a physical reducing isometry. The old revision note/audit remain visibly historical.

are

corrections.correction: Replace 'no-count propagator' by 'no-count effect', or replace that formula by K0(u)=exp(-gamma*u/2)I and separately state F_u(ready)=K0* K0=exp(-gamma*u)I. First-count effects remain gamma*exp(-gamma*s)*P_a ds.
